contexts.text: Hence they seemed to themselves to be more learned than others.
They suppose that in the other life the learned shall shine like the stars... But the learned... = those who are in good...
It has been given to speak with the more learned concerning this...
(The stupid ignorance of a certain learned Church dignitary.)
The learned in the Ancient Church knew that...
Such appear to themselves learned and wise. AC 5433:2.
Sorcerers = those who are learned from themselves... For he who will be learned in the truths and goods of faith, must be taught by the Lord...
They wondered that those who, above others, had been learned in the Word and in the doctrine of their Church, were among the damned...
Those who are learned as to doctrine, but evil as to life, are meant in... ; ; and also by the foolish virgins.
In the external form... they appear equally as intelligent and learned as those who are in the light of Heaven...
They had persuaded themselves that they should come into Heaven... because they had been learned...
I knew a man ordinarily learned...
If they have been learned, they apply scientifics to confirm the proprium of man and nature.
The exploration and manifestation of the state of life of those in the Church of the Reformed, who are called learned and wise from the confirmation of faith separated from charity... Signified.
Thus do the simple, ... but rarely the learned and erudite.
A company where were the learned and erudite...
All these (who wore hats) were learned and erudite; and some, who wore turbans, were unlearned. They were speaking together about unlimited Divine power...
At the left were seen the learned of the clergy, and behind them the unlearned; and at the right the erudite of the laity, and behind them the inerudite...
That the learned and erudite who have confirmed themselves deeply in falsities... are sensuous above others... TCR 565.
One of the spheres is concerning the Lord, which breathes forth from the southern quarter, where are the learned of the clergy, and the erudite of the laity...
Cunning and malignant Spirits seduce the learned, and philosophers, more easily than others...
Concerning a certain one among the most learned.
That those who suppose themselves to be in the greatest light, because they are learned, will be in the greatest darkness. Representation.
That the learned, who are exterior men, apprehend nothing but exterior things.
Those who represent the learned, or the wise of the world... wanted my tongue to perish. Explained.
That truths... not sensuous... are at once rejected by the learned.
That the learned in the world obscure the understanding of man.
a. That the learned are not permitted to speak with Spirits, except with danger to their lives.
That the most learned... have conceived a false idea of Heaven.
That the learned who have taken up phantasies, see nothing else than the things which confirm them.
Therefore, in the learned the ideas are closed...
Therefore, the unlearned... can often think and speak better than the learned...
The things from which he had been learned...
They brought the stupid, who in the world had been the learned.
Concerning those who are called and believed to be learned...
Concerning the learned of this age.
This is not to be learned, that is, illustrated.
I have seen many, even of the most learned, cast into Hell.
Hence it is that the learned of the Church, when they come into the Spiritual World, are in so many falsities, that they know scarcely one genuine truth.
Provided (the English) are persuaded that he is a learned and sincere man...
